newsitem.title: ITALY: Italian shares end lower, braked by profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: Italian shares end lower, braked by profit-taking.

text.p: Italian shares closed lower but above session troughs on Thursday with the rally of recent days petering out for the moment on selective profit-taking which dealers said demonstrated signs of emerging nervousness.
Industrials like Montedison were penalised despite the agri-chemical group's positive outlook for 1997. It closed off 1.82 percent at 1,131 lire.
The all-share Mibtel index ended 0.46 percent lower at 13,407 after a 13,335-13,465 range. The Mib30 blue chip index ended 0.49 percent down at 20,384 after a 20,262-20,499 range.

Food group Parmalat ended 3.89 percent down at 2,373 lire on London-originated selling with operators perplexed at the group's intended investment in the North American market which is perceived as saturated, dealers said.
State-controlled energy group ENI lost 0.63 percent to 9,648 ahead of the last day on Friday of its third tranche public share offer.
Car maker Fiat slipped 0.73 percent to 6,145 and troubled information and technology group Olivetti fell 3.69 percent to 482.5.
In the telecoms sector, Telecom Italia was flat at 5,663 and mobile phone operator TIM lost 2.36 percent to 5,632.
In banks, Banco Ambrosiano Veneto, firm all day, put on 2.83 percent to 4827 lire as its proposed merger with savings bank Cariplo was perceived to be getting near.

Savings bank Cassa di Risparmio di Verona said it was selling its 12.62 percent stake in Ambroveneto. While the stake is to be offered first to other Ambroveneto shareholders, they are deemed unlikely to take it up and so operators expected Cariplo's controlling foundation would buy the stake.
